# Appendix A. Historical Run Registry and Coverage Reconciliation

This appendix records the historical run inventories used by the report and
the later reconciliation of those inventories. Sections A.1–A.5 are not an
exhaustive current account history. Section A.11 is the 19 October 2026
export of the account's training-run, W&B, and Hugging Face Hub logging records. Provider
logging identities, independent scientific executions, checkpoint revisions,
and claim-to-run links are different units and must not be added as though
they were interchangeable. Run identifier,
library and platform, base model, algorithm, group size, dataset, seed, steps,
and terminal status are retained where a primary source records them; unknown
fields remain unknown. A claim without supporting primary evidence must be
qualified or withdrawn rather than inferred from an inventory count.

Historical inventories differ in scope and counting units. Provider-ledger entries, opening-study records, claim links and independent scientific trials are not interchangeable. Sections A.1–A.5 retain scientific study configurations, denominators, outcomes and limitations, and they make no complete-coverage claim. Section A.11 is a separate 19 October 2026 logging export of the owned Tinker training runs, the W&B runs visible to the same account, and the Hugging Face Hub repositories visible to the same account. Those rows are logging records. They are not additional independent trials, and they do not change the claim tiers in Section A.3.

## A.1 Historical boundary and source scope

The Semester-3 boundary is the public tag `capstone-final-2026-04-25`, commit `21a99ef7` dated 23 April 2026. Attribution of inherited and individual work rests on commit history, not provider-account ownership or activity counts. The study tables below retain scientific configurations, seeds, steps, outcomes and evidence tiers. Operational identifiers are withheld; locally named scientific study units remain for interpretation.

**Table A.1 — Historical source scope in the public derivative.**

| Source category | Public interpretation |
|---|---|
| Historical provider-ledger snapshots | Source-accounting records, not independent experiment counts; account breakdowns are omitted |
| Scientific study records | Reported configurations, seeds, steps, outcomes and limitations appear in the following study tables |

: Historical source scope; no account-level project census is included.

## A.2 Semester-3 shared benchmark runs

The Semester-3 contribution was the multi-framework benchmark infrastructure:
a common harness, a fixed evaluation configuration, and integrations for
several independent RL post-training libraries. These runs are the shared
baseline measurements, and they are the ones for which the registry is *most*
complete, because each was produced under a declared configuration.

**Table A.2 — Cross-framework comparison at the fixed benchmark configuration.**
Configuration for all four rows: model `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` (Tinker row uses
`Qwen/Qwen3-8B-Base`), algorithm GRPO, group size G = 8, learning rate 1e-5,
dataset GSM8K[:500], 30 steps, seed 42. Metric is `last10_avg`, the mean of
the final ten reported training rewards. Source:
`platform_hybrid/experiments/results/framework_comparison.json`, generated by
`aggregate_framework_comparison.py`.

| `modal_trl_trl_qwen3_8b` | TRL on Modal H100 | Qwen/Qwen3-8B | GRPO | 8 | gsm8k-500 | 42 | 30 | last10 = 0.05, 735.7 s — **real run** |

The two `dryrun` rows are a documented threat to validity, not a result: the
generator falls back to a deterministic seeded trace from `verl.VERLTrainer` /
`OpenRLHFTrainer` when the framework is absent from the sandbox, and the JSON
carries the note "Seeded deterministic fallback … (verl not installed in
sandbox)". Any comparison reading them as measurements of verl or OpenRLHF is
invalid. The Tinker row also initialises from the *base* checkpoint while the
open-framework rows use the instruction-tuned one, so even the two real rows
are not a clean framework contrast.

Three facts here are load-bearing. First, **no empirical headline row in the
P1–P8 ledger reaches Tier A or B** under the statistical-rigor thresholds; the
rectified P1–P8 tally is C = 12, R = 2, X = 4. P11 adds an eight-seed
matched block but does not meet the stated Tier A step threshold, as
clarified below. Second, the four Tier X rows are
X for specific, checkable reasons: **P3-C2** rests on G = 32 *sampling* cells
with zero optimizer steps, so no matched G = 4/G = 32 training replication
exists; **P4-C1**'s abstract names Qwen3-8B while every mapped run is
`Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct`; **P5-C1** compares `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-Base` against
`Qwen/Qwen3-8B`, so the base checkpoint changes together with the backend and
the pair must not be cited as a backend-only causal effect; and **P8-C3** is a
proposed architecture with no execution, hence zero linked runs. Third, some cross-provider model-identity conflicts remain unresolved. Their private identity reconciliation is outside this public package; the affected scientific model-attribution claims remain contested.

Two column caveats travel with the table. The dataset cell for P7-C1 is `—`
because the ledger's only dataset-adjacent field for those 368 runs is a
prompt/tokenizer family (`llama3`, `qwen3_instruct`, `gpt_oss_low_reasoning`,
`nemotron3_disable_thinking`), not a dataset name. And the P3 sweep here is
**not** the Semester-3 sweep of Table A.4: it is a different project
(`study logging group`), a different model (Qwen3.5-4B), and it reports deltas of
0.0000 rather than held-out accuracies near 0.99. The two share a group-size
grid and nothing else. Chapters 4 and 6 cite the Table A.4 sweep (Qwen2.5-0.5B)
whenever they give the 0.838 → 0.631 ZVF decline or the 0.98–0.99 held-out
figures. They do not cite P3-C1.

The extension ledger added in August 2026 carries five rows besides P11:
P10-C1 is Tier R (an algebraic identity, not an empirical result), P10-C2 and
P12-C2 are Tier X (placeholder figures and unlinked prospective claims, zero
runs), and P12-C1 is Tier R as a lemma and Tier X as an empirical headline.

**P11** is an eight-seed, matched-stack block of 40 arm–seed units at
`local:zvf-program/audit/results/full/{grpo,dapo,gspo,drgrpo,aero}-seed-{11,23,37,53,71,89,107,131}.json`,
five arms × eight seeds on one stack (Qwen3-8B, GSM8K, 30 steps, Colab A100,
held-out n = 500). Its headline contrast, DAPO versus GRPO, is Δ = +0.001,
percentile-bootstrap CI [−0.0045, +0.00675] (paired-t 95% CI [−0.0063, +0.0083], n = 8 seeds; the bootstrap undercovers at this n), MDE₈₀ = 0.01012, all raw p > 0.21, with
Benjamini–Hochberg rejecting nothing. The mechanism is visible in the
diagnostic: DAPO's mean ZVF is 0.000 against GRPO's 0.693, bought with 3.61×
the rollouts (1,734 versus 480) and 1.44× the wall clock. This eight-paired-seed contrast has no multiplicity-adjusted rejection and does not establish equivalence. Every retained P11 final manifest specifies
`max_steps=30`; the 40 units are 30-step runs. Accordingly this block does
**not** satisfy the stated Tier A requirement of at least 100 steps per run
and remains Tier C under the vocabulary above. Pooling steps across arms or
seeds does not satisfy that per-run requirement. This corrects the evidence
tier, not the recorded rewards, seed counts, interval, or null result.

### A.3.1 Opening and null-result runs

Chapter 6 reports four null families — a mixed-variance curriculum, a matched
token budget, hard-prompt filtering, and step-1 layer selection (§6.4.3) — and
each rests on source-specific scientific result records rather than an account-wide inventory. The study The
rows are counted from the per-run `name` (or mode) fields of
each artefact's JSON — `results.json` for the curriculum, token-budget,
hard-prompt and loss-formulation blocks, `result.json` and its siblings for
P1 — not from an inventory API, which is why this cohort is reported as its
own total. Three neighbouring blocks add nothing to
it: the P3 group-size artefacts are already indexed — `groupsize_zvf/results.json`
reproduces the per-group deltas of Table A.5's P3-C1 row exactly, and the
second sweep file is discussed below — and the P2, P7 and P8 "openings"
(`p2_openings/collapse_baseline_analysis.json`, `p7_controller/sim.json`,
`p8_openings/*.json`) are zero-compute re-analyses that launch no runs.

Three provenance notes belong with this table, because two of its blocks carry
superseded siblings and one carries a refuted claim. First,
`campaign/FINDINGS.md` describes a nine-run, three-seed version of the campaign
on a twelve-prompt held-out set with arm means of +0.028 and −0.028;
`campaign/results.json` holds fifteen runs over six seeds on a thirty-prompt
held-out set (0.8667 = 26/30), and the table follows the per-run file. The
FINDINGS warning that `zero_loss_frac` was invalid (an empty-metrics-dict bug,
"since fixed") belongs to the nine-run batch, not to that file. Second, the P1
layer-freeze block has the same shape: the two-seed 3B pass (overlap
0.1111 ± 0.0000) is superseded by the four-seed pass (0.0833 ± 0.0481), and
the larger-model overlap is below the simple independent 0.25 reference, so the toy-scale overlap of 1.0 must not be read as a
transferable layer-selection signal. Third, the two single-seed training
blocks flagged SUSPECT by independent verification (kimi, 2026-07-06) are
superseded by the multi-seed blocks above: the curriculum opening's +0.05
(campaign curriculum and baseline arms separate by 0.006 over six seeds, at
3.3–7.2× oversample cost), and a single-seed G = 4 gain of +0.125 in `p3_groupsize/sweep_results.json`
— the campaign's G4 seed-0 baseline gains 0.0000, not 0.125, and that sweep
file retains only two of its twelve entries, so the W&B group is its record.

## A.4 E1–E14 evaluation campaign lanes

The fourteen evaluation lanes are not training runs; they are evaluations of a
single frozen actor, and they carry the registry's strictest receipt
discipline. The actor is base `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` (commit `995ad96e…`) with
adapter `campaign-adapter`
(commit `withheld-adapter-revision…`), bfloat16, trained on Tinker, run seed 809 taken from the
adapter name. The adapter was trained for 40 steps at G = 4 and learning rate
1 × 10⁻⁵ by REINFORCE with a group-mean baseline (no KL, no clipping), as
recorded in the local W&B run directory for run [identifier withheld] and the run receipt
`withheld actor-training receipt`
(Chapter 8 §8.1.1). Those are properties of the single actor rather than of
any lane, and every lane carries the same run seed (809), so algorithm, group size, seed and step columns are omitted from Table A.8. Terminal states are from the ledger of record,

## A.5 Completeness limitations

The historical registry is an index of its retained snapshot and is incomplete as a scientific dataset. Many records lack model, dataset, algorithm, group size, steps or a usable outcome. Missing fields remain unknown; names and provider state are not used to infer them. Section A.11 lists the live logging export. Missing scientific fields in that export stay unknown; a provider state or a display name is not used to fill them.

**Table A.9 — Scientific metadata limitations.**

| Required scientific field | Interpretation of missing data |
|---|---|
| Model and dataset | Do not infer identity from a display name or tokenizer family |
| Algorithm and group size | An unrecorded configuration remains unknown |
| Training steps | Provider state does not establish completed optimization |
| Outcome | A logged record without a metric is not a scored scientific result |

: Metadata limitations in the historical retained registry; private account-level field counts are omitted.

Four further limits apply.

1. **Aggregate presentation.** This appendix names 105 runs individually: the 4
   cross-framework runs of Table A.2, the 20 Modal campaign runs of A.3, the 12
   sweep runs (in 4 rows) of A.4, the 46 opening runs (in 16 rows) of A.6, and
   the 23 E-lane rows of A.8 — plus the 18 claim rows of Table A.5, which index
   claims rather than runs.
   Other historical inventory entries are outside this 105-row subtotal. Section A.11 lists the later live logging export separately and does not add those rows to the 105.

2. **Non-runs inside the count.** Three entries are not training results:
   `verl-dryrun` and `openrlhf-dryrun` are seeded deterministic fallbacks, and
   the E4 reported base-model rerun is an unverified secondary account; to these add
   §A.3.1's P1 gradient probe, which takes no optimizer steps at all. They are
   included as historical record rows, not as evidence of completed training
   or of the excluded E4 execution.

3. **Identity conflicts.** Historical source-identity disagreements remain a limitation; private provider reconciliation and its counts are withheld.

4. **Snapshot scope.** Historical source inventories differ in scope. They are not counts of independent experiments. Section A.11 is the 19 October 2026 replay of the live logging export; it is not a recount of the historical subtotal.

Named artifacts may preserve an arithmetic result while missing source identity limits attribution to an algorithm or checkpoint. Chapters 6–8 state each claim's verification level; selected audits are not universal verification. The registry records reported provenance and
identity, shows that the run population is far larger than the reported
claims, and shows that those claims rest on a small, explicitly tiered subset
with the P1–P8 empirical rows at Tier C or X and P11 at Tier C under the
stated per-run step threshold. The four Tier X P1–P8 rows must not be cited
as supporting evidence under their conflicted labels. Two are nevertheless
cited elsewhere in a restricted form, and the restriction is part of the
citation: P4-C1 is cited only under the model its runs actually record
(`Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct` in every row of `results/drgrpo_gsm8k_cot_full.json`),
never under the Qwen3-8B label of the P4 source abstract; P5-C1 (0.856 versus
0.050) is cited only as an under-specification exhibit whose checkpoint and
back-end changed together, never as a back-end effect. P3-C2 and P8-C3 are not
cited as evidence anywhere.

The run totals that appear in different chapters count different corpora. Table A.10 lists the scientific study corpora retained publicly.
